I calculated the Q3 results and saved them to `/work/answer.json`. Before running Q3, I ran the same code on Q2 and it reproduced all 10 reference values exactly.

**Q3 results (Jul 1 – Sep 30, 2025)**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| a. Highest net-revenue segment | `smb`, 290,576,683 KRW |
| b. Customers with paid orders | 248 |
| c. Highest net-revenue category | `sw`, 324,945,545 KRW |
| d. Highest net-revenue month | 2025-09 |
| e. Customer with the largest total refunds | u165@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2+ paid orders | 234 |
| g. Average net revenue per order | 681,477 KRW |
| h. September growth over August | 1.1% |

**Interpretation choices I had to make**
The data had quirks the definitions don't cover, so I tried each plausible reading on Q2. Only one combination matched all 10 reference values:

1. **Timezone:** `ordered_at` is stored in UTC (`...Z`). Dates and months are only correct after converting to Korea time (UTC+9). Using UTC as-is, 7 of the values were off.
2. **Counting customers:** there are 300 customer records but only 250 distinct emails, because 50 customers have two records each. A customer has to be counted once per email (lowercased, spaces trimmed) for b, e and f to match. Counting by `customers.id` gives 282 for b in Q2.
3. **Segment values:** values like `' consumer'`, `'Enterprise '` and `'SMB'` have stray spaces and mixed case. I trimmed and lowercased them before grouping.

Other details:
- The 2025-04 month is empty because the data starts on 2025-05-01. For h, I compared months by name (month 2 vs month 3 of the quarter) rather than by position.
- h uses exact decimal arithmetic with half-up rounding.

The script is `/work/analyze.py`. Running `python3 analyze.py 9 email` checks Q2, then recalculates Q3 and writes `answer.json`.
